## Solution

We compute the Smith normal form of the relation matrix. The relations are the rows of

$$M = \begin{pmatrix} 9 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Step 1.** Swap rows 1 and 2 to bring the entry $3$ (smallest nonzero) to position $(1,1)$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & -3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Step 2.** Clear column 1 below the pivot: $R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 3R_1$, $R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - R_1$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Step 3.** Clear column 1 to the right: $C_2 \leftarrow C_2 - C_1$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Step 4.** Eliminate the third row: $R_3 \leftarrow R_3 - R_2$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

**Step 5.** Clear column 3 using column 2: $C_3 \leftarrow C_3 + C_2$:

$$\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

Make all diagonal entries non-negative:

$$\operatorname{diag}(3,\, 6,\, 0).$$

**Verification via minors.** The gcd of all entries of $M$ is $\gcd(9,3,6,3,3,0,3,-3,6)=3$, giving $d_1 = 3$. The $2\times 2$ minors are $18, 18, 18, 36, 36, 36, 18, 18, 18$, whose gcd is $18 = d_1 d_2$, so $d_2 = 6$. The full determinant is $0$, so $d_3 = 0$ and the rank is $2$. This confirms the Smith normal form $\operatorname{diag}(3, 6, 0)$.

**Decomposition.** The invariant factors $3, 6, 0$ give

$$A \cong \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}.$$

Since $6 = 2\cdot 3$ with $\gcd(2,3)=1$, we have $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$. Decomposing into cyclic groups of prime order or infinite order:

$$\boxed{A \cong \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}.}$$
